topline.text: The government has confirmed the biggest overhaul of school food standards in over a decade — capping high fat, salt and sugar foods and requiring more fresh fruit, veg and wholegrains — with schools given a year to prepare before the rules bite in September 2027.
topline.action: A long lead-in, but worth flagging to catering and finance teams now given the scale of the menu changes required.

topline.text: Ofsted's latest round of Sheffield inspections (rounded up by The Star this week) is a mixed bag: praise for schools like Swallownest Primary and Bankwood Community, but a critical report for Stocksbridge High School over attendance and outcomes for disadvantaged pupils.
topline.action: A useful local comparator if you're benchmarking attendance or disadvantage-gap language in your own SEF.

diary.text: DfE's twin SEND/EOTAS reform consultations close — last call to respond before proposals are firmed up.

items.lede: Biggest school food shake-up in a decade.
items.body: New standards will limit food and drink high in fat, salt and sugar and put more fresh fruit, vegetables and wholegrains on every plate. Schools have a year to prepare before the rules take effect in September 2027, with some secondary-specific measures phased in by 2028.
items.action: Long lead-in, but a good moment to start the catering-contract conversation.

items.lede: Nine Sheffield schools and nurseries get fresh Ofsted ratings.
items.body: The Star's latest roundup covers inspections from the summer through to the first week of September: Swallownest Primary and Bankwood Community were both praised, while Stocksbridge High School was criticised over 'unacceptable' attendance and disadvantaged pupils leaving without basic qualifications.
items.action: Worth a read if any partner schools are due inspection soon — a live sense of what's landing hardest under the current framework.

items.body: The inquiry into failures at the Countess of Chester Hospital reported this week; the Health Secretary called it "thorough and devastating" and pledged action on whistleblowing and information-sharing failures. It's an NHS story, not a schools one, but it lands the same week the DfE's own information-sharing duty comes into focus ahead of its 30 September commencement.
items.action: Not schools-specific, but useful background if your safeguarding lead is reviewing how concerns get escalated and shared across agencies.

box.label: Jargon-buster - EOTAS
box.intro: Cropping up a lot as the DfE's SEND consultations close this Friday.
box.text: "Education Otherwise Than At School" — the legal route for children who can't attend a mainstream or special school placement. The current consultation asks whether it should also cover some children no longer eligible for an EHCP.
